title: Brand and customers
hired_for: To tell the owner who really buys, why, and in what words, and what stops the rest, so every ad, page and email speaks to real people and wastes less money.

jobs.job: Tell me who really buys from us and why, with proof from orders and reviews
jobs.why: Ads, pages and emails built for an imagined customer waste money. The owner needs the real buyer groups, the job each one hires the product for, and the evidence behind it.

watch.metric: share of last 90 days revenue from buyers who match a buyer profile backed by at least 5 real quotes
watch.source: Shopify orders and reviews, with profiles in the brand brain

drives.metric: conversion rate on ads and pages built for a named profile

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 1 profile, written from a guess, covers nobody we can count. After: 3 profiles with quotes cover 70% of revenue and the next ad round is briefed to them.
jobs.who_today: founder or agency strategist, from memory

jobs.job: Use my customers' own words in ads and pages instead of guessing
jobs.why: Buyers respond to the words they use for their own problem. Copy written in marketing words gets scrolled past.

watch.metric: click-through rate on ads that use a customer phrase against ads that do not, 14 days
watch.source: Meta Ads Manager, with the phrase bank in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 1 in 10 live ads uses a real customer phrase. After: 6 in 10 do, and click-through on those runs 25% higher.

jobs.job: Know what customers love and hate from reviews, before it hurts sales
jobs.why: Reviews show what is breaking long before revenue does. A new complaint theme left alone turns into returns and lower star ratings.

watch.metric: average star rating and share of 1 to 2 star reviews by theme, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 9% of new reviews mention thin fabric, up from 2%, and nobody has read them. After: the theme is flagged in week 1 and sent to the supplier.

jobs.job: Pair every reason people do not buy with the thing that removes it
jobs.why: Each doubt that is not answered on the page costs sales. The owner needs the top doubts, and the proof that actually clears each one.

watch.metric: product page add to cart rate, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 'will they fall down' is the top doubt in 40 reviews and not answered on the page. After: a fit guarantee and 3 matching reviews go above the fold and add to cart rises 12%.

jobs.job: See which buyer groups come back and which buy once
jobs.why: Buyers who come back are worth 3 to 5 times more. Spending the same to win a one-time buyer as a loyal one wastes budget.

watch.metric: repeat purchase rate at 90 days by buyer group

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: all buyers get the same ads and emails. After: the group with 38% repeat gets 2 times the budget and repeat revenue grows 15% in 2 quarters.

jobs.job: Know which buyer groups make the most gross profit, not just revenue
jobs.why: A group that buys a lot on discount can make less money than a smaller group that pays full price. Budget should follow profit.

watch.metric: gross profit per customer at 180 days, by buyer group and first product
watch.source: Shopify orders, refunds and cost per item

drives.metric: gross profit per dollar of ad spend

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the discount buyer group is the biggest by revenue. After: it shows the lowest profit per customer, and its share of ad budget drops from 40% to 20%.

jobs.job: Find the top reasons behind returns and support tickets
jobs.why: Returns and tickets are buyers telling you what went wrong. Each fixed cause cuts refunds, support cost and bad reviews.

watch.metric: share of returns and tickets by reason, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 31% of returns say 'too tight' with no size advice on the page. After: a fit guide and size note cut that reason by half in 60 days.

jobs.job: Say clearly who the product is wrong for, to cut returns
jobs.why: Selling to people the product does not suit brings returns and angry reviews. A plain 'not for' line saves both.

watch.metric: returns marked 'not as expected' or 'did not suit', 60 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 12% of returns say 'not what I expected'. After: a 'not for you if' line on 3 product pages brings it to 7%.

jobs.job: Check every claim has proof before it goes live
jobs.why: A claim with no proof can bring a legal letter, an ad account ban or a loss of trust. It has to be checked before it ships, not after.

watch.metric: live claims with no proof on file
watch.source: claims list in the brand brain, checked against live ads and pages

drives.metric: ads rejected or accounts restricted for claims, per quarter

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 4 live ads say 'clinically proven' with no study on file. After: 0 unproven claims, and 2 are reworded with the real test result.

jobs.job: Catch a spike in bad mentions before it spreads
jobs.why: A bad post or a product problem can spread in hours. A quick, honest reply keeps it small.

watch.metric: negative comments and tickets about one topic in 24 hours, against normal
watch.source: Meta page comments and Gorgias social tickets

drives.metric: star rating and repeat rate over the next 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a shipping delay post gets 200 angry comments before anyone replies. After: a reply is up within 2 hours and comments slow the same day.

jobs.job: Learn what made new buyers choose us
jobs.why: The owner needs to know what moved the buyer: a friend, an ad, a review or a gift. That tells them where to spend and what to say.

watch.metric: share of new customers by reason and first place they heard of us, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 35% of new buyers say a friend told them and there is no referral offer. After: a referral offer goes live and brings 8% of new customers in a quarter.

jobs.job: Know the moment that makes someone buy, so ads and emails land on time
jobs.why: People buy when something happens: a new job, a race, a cold snap, running out. Messages timed to that moment get more buyers for the same spend.

watch.metric: email click rate on messages timed to a buying moment, 30 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: all emails go on a fixed weekly calendar. After: a 'first cold week' send by region gets 2 times the click rate.

jobs.job: Know if the brand is getting stronger or weaker, apart from any one campaign
jobs.why: Ads can hide a weakening brand for a while. When fewer people search for the brand by name, every sale gets more expensive.

watch.metric: branded search clicks, 4 weeks against the same weeks last year

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: branded search down 11% over 8 weeks while ad spend held flat. After: the drop is flagged in week 3 and a word-of-mouth push brings it back up in a quarter.

jobs.job: Show each shopper the proof and reviews from people like them
jobs.why: A runner and a nurse buy the same sock for different reasons. Showing each the reviews that match them makes the proof believable.

watch.metric: product page conversion rate by traffic source, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: every visitor sees the same 5 reviews. After: ad traffic for nurses lands on reviews from nurses and converts 18% better.

jobs.job: Test a message on a buyer profile before spending real money on it
jobs.why: Many ads fail in the first 3 days. A quick check against the buyer profile weeds out weak ideas before any spend.

watch.metric: share of new ads that beat the account's median click-through rate in 7 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 3 in 10 new ads beat the median. After: weak ones are cut before launch and 5 in 10 beat it.

jobs.job: Split one broad buyer into separate profiles when the reason to buy is different
jobs.why: One average customer fits nobody. When 2 groups buy for different reasons, one message serves both badly.

watch.metric: buyer profiles with their own reason to buy, quote set and revenue share

drives.metric: conversion rate on ads built per profile

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 1 profile for all buyers. After: gift buyers and everyday wearers are split, each with its own ads, and gift season revenue grows 20%.

jobs.job: Keep buyer profiles fresh and recheck them every 90 days
jobs.why: Buyers change with price moves, new products and new channels. An old profile sends ads to people who no longer buy.

watch.metric: buyer profiles rechecked against orders and reviews in the last 90 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the main profile was last checked 11 months ago. After: it is rechecked each quarter and a new age group is added.

jobs.job: Keep the brand voice current and check each asset before it ships
jobs.why: When every freelancer writes in their own voice, the brand sounds like 5 brands. Buyers trust a brand that sounds the same everywhere.

watch.metric: share of new ads, pages and emails that pass the voice check before launch
watch.source: voice sheet in the brand brain, checked against Meta, Shopify and Klaviyo copy

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 6 in 10 new assets pass. After: 9 in 10 pass and edits per asset drop from 3 rounds to 1.

jobs.job: Talk to customers every week so research never goes stale
jobs.why: Reviews and data say what happened. Talking to buyers says why. Without it, profiles drift into guesses.

watch.metric: customer calls or message chats logged per month

drives.metric: buyer profiles backed by first-hand quotes

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 0 calls in 6 months. After: 4 a month, and 2 new doubts are added to the page in the first quarter.

jobs.job: Watch for anyone taking our name, web address or social handles
jobs.why: A copycat store, a lookalike domain or a lost handle confuses buyers and steals sales. It is cheap to catch early and costly to fix late.

watch.metric: open alerts on lookalike domains, handles and trademark filings
watch.source: trademark and domain watch in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: a lookalike store runs ads with our photos for 3 weeks. After: it is flagged in 2 days and taken down in a week.

jobs.job: Find a buyer group nobody else is chasing
jobs.why: When every rival targets the same buyer, ads get dear. A group nobody serves can be won at a lower cost.

watch.metric: cost per purchase on ads built for the new buyer group, 14 days

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: all ads target active adults, like 7 rivals. After: an ad set for people on their feet all day at work runs at 30% lower cost per purchase.

jobs.job: Walk the site, ads and emails as a shopper to catch where the brand has drifted
jobs.why: Small changes by many hands pull the brand off course. A regular walk-through catches mixed messages and broken steps.

watch.metric: journey checks passed on the last walk-through
watch.source: walk-through log in the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the ad promises free returns and the checkout page charges $5. After: the walk-through finds it and the page is fixed the same week.

jobs.job: See if customers describe us the way we describe ourselves
jobs.why: If we say 'premium comfort' and buyers say 'good value', ads aimed at the wrong idea waste money.

watch.metric: share of review and survey words that match our stated main message, quarter
watch.source: review app and post-purchase survey, with the message in the brand brain

drives.metric: click-through rate on ads that lead with the buyers' words

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 15% of review words match our main message. After: the message is rewritten from buyer words and ad click-through rises 10%.

jobs.job: Confirm a research finding holds for many buyers, not just the ones we read
jobs.why: A finding from 20 reviews can be wrong. A short survey to hundreds of buyers checks it before the brand bets on it.

watch.metric: share of survey answers that confirm the finding, with at least 200 replies

drives.metric: share of briefs built on confirmed findings

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: the brand bets a campaign on 'gift buyers' from 12 reviews. After: a 400 reply survey shows gifts are 9% of orders and the budget moves.

jobs.job: Keep every page and channel leading with the same one idea
jobs.why: When the home page, ads and emails each lead with a different message, none of them sticks.

watch.metric: share of live pages, ads and emails that lead with the current main message
watch.source: Shopify pages, Meta ads and Klaviyo emails, checked against the brand brain

jobs.now_after: Example: Now: 4 different lead messages across 5 channels. After: all 5 lead with 1 message for a quarter.
